scenes.say: How does coffee lose its caffeine? There are three ways, and they all share one step.
Decaf starts as green coffee, which means raw, unroasted beans. The caffeine comes out first, and only then are the beans roasted.
The first method uses water. The beans soak in hot water, and a carbon filter catches the caffeine from that water. The same water can be reused on the next batch.
The second method uses a solvent, such as ethyl acetate. It picks up the caffeine, and then it is steamed or evaporated off the beans.
The third method uses carbon dioxide. Moistened beans go into a pressurized vessel, where the carbon dioxide draws out the caffeine and usually leaves most other compounds behind.
So every decaf follows the same three moves: green beans, caffeine pulled out, then a normal roast.
Decaf is made on green beans, using water, a solvent or carbon dioxide. Save this for later.
